case_title: R. Shaji v. State of Kerala
aggravating_circumstances: Motive established, use of vehicle, dismemberment of body, conspiracy
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment
offence_finally_established: Murder, criminal conspiracy, criminal trespass, and causing disappearance of a person
neutral_facts: The accused, a police officer, was involved in the murder of a victim who had developed an intimate relationship with the accused's wife. The victim was last seen with the accused and another individual. A chopper used in the dismemberment of the victim's body was recovered at the behest of the accused. The victim's body parts were found in a lake, and a DNA report confirmed the identity of the victim. The accused and another person were involved in a conspiracy to eliminate the victim. The prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence, including witness statements, recovery of items, and the victim's injuries as revealed by the post-mortem report. The accused's knowledge of the victim's relationship with his wife and his threats against the victim were key elements of the prosecution's case.
